$comment: Source of truth for the import layering. A layer may import its own layer and the layers below it. Checked by dependency-cruiser (.dependency-cruiser.mjs) and scripts/check-architecture.mjs; the TypeScript projects (tsconfig.layer-*.json) mirror it; the AGENTS.md layer table is generated from this file (npm run gen:structure-doc). `packages` are folders with a public surface: a HIGHER layer may import them only through an entry (type-only `import()` queries and dynamic `import()` of lazy entries excepted); same-layer and lower-layer code, and tests, may reach inside.

layers.name: foundation
layers.note: Pure data, constants, the numeric layer. Imports nothing above.

layers.name: state
layers.note: External stores and the debug surface (window globals, probe shapes).

layers.name: engine
layers.note: GPU, audio, XR, capability manifest, Maps/routing services, offline trips.

layers.name: car
layers.note: The cabin: lazy car runtime, cabin renderer, input.

layers.name: ui
layers.note: React: hooks, components, views, the app shell.

wasm.note: The loader plus its typed facades. abi.ts / marshal.ts / bindExports.ts are internal.

renderer.note: What the cabin and the UI use of the road renderer: backend, probes, registries, stats stores. Does not export the lazy entries (SemanticController, WebGL2FallbackRenderer).

car.note: eager.ts is safe from main-bundle code. index.ts is the lazy-side API: it re-exports carModeRuntime, so only code the lazy car chunk reaches may import it (scripts/check-architecture.mjs enforces).
